title: Iterative Prompting
outcome: By the end, I can revise one prompt component and compare paired outputs using the same rubric.
scenario: A fictional Study Buddy prompt invents a definition when approved notes omit it.
given: P asks “answer helpfully”. Revision Q adds “if approved notes lack the answer, say not supplied”.
Hold model settings and four development questions fixed. P passes 1,2; Q passes 1,2,3. Case 4 still fails.

steps.label: Locate failure
steps.detail: The target defect is unsupported answers when notes are missing.

steps.label: One controlled change
steps.detail: Q adds the missing-evidence rule; other instructions remain fixed.

steps.label: Paired results
steps.detail: P=2/4; Q=3/4; gain is case 3, with case 4 unresolved.

steps.label: Next action
steps.detail: Inspect case 4 and reserve genuinely fresh questions for final evaluation.

explanation: An iteration should respond to a recorded failure with a precise change. Comparing the same questions reveals whether other behavior changed too. The invented results show a development gain of one case, not a guarantee that the new instruction always works. Save prompt text, settings, source notes and case-level outcomes.

counterfactual.change: Change model settings and note wording at the same time as the prompt.
counterfactual.prediction: The comparison no longer isolates the prompt revision.
counterfactual.reason: Several changes could explain the altered outputs; record them or run separate controlled comparisons.

student_task: What evidence supports improvement here, and what remains unproven?
teacher_answer: Q gains case 3 without losing 1 or 2 on this four-case record; 4 still fails and new-case performance remains unknown.
project_evidence: Maintain a Study Buddy experiment log linking failure, single revision and paired rubric results.
limits: Stochastic output can vary across runs; a small comparison does not prove an average effect or classroom learning benefit.
review_note: Individually designed fictional worked case, distinct from the reserved assessment. Toy model simplifications, arithmetic and source authority reviewed explicitly.
